messages:
lina: quick sync — sales pushed back asking for a per-region guaranteed throughput add-on. they want EU/US capacity carved out with SLA. do we productize as an addon sku or a per-route SLA flag?
ethan: leaning addon. aligns with dedicated/reserved concept and simpler to bill. enforcement boundaries are the main concern.
maya: addon is fine if router actually enforces isolation. otherwise shared pool gets noisy and customers will complain. also need clear burst vs sustained semantics.
cheng: sales feedback: customers want per-region invoicing for compliance and egress/legal clarity. so prefer separate line items per region.
ash: implementation notes from infra: two main patterns: token-bucket per-tenant-per-region (fast) OR per-route priority queues + reservation (more changes). token-bucket easiest to ship but less expressive for route-level SLAs.
lina: proposed launch checklist: 1) billable SKU per-region throughput 2) router enforcement + safe fallback (degrade to shared pool with throttled fallback) 3) docs + migration playbook from soft-credit to hard-addon 4) 2-customer canary
ethan: add success metric: p95 tail latency <= 150ms when addon utilization >= 90%. also surface cost delta per 1k tokens in pricing docs.
maya: agree on p95. also require model-variant transparency: if we fallback to a cheaper model or reroute, emit telemetry and customer event so they see quality changes.
sales-ops-bot: note — two enterprise prospects asked specifically for EU throughput guarantees. potential TCV ~ $1.2M/yr if we can ship EU SLA and contract carveouts.
cheng: pricing shape options: flat monthly slab + linear overage OR tiered buckets. sales likes tiered buckets for negotiations but slab+overage is simpler for forecasting.
ash: capacity implication: hard slabbing needs reservation in Dedicated GPU pools or soft reservation with autoscaling signals. both require improved capacity forecasting to avoid naked promises.
lina: risks: missing enforcement -> SLA breaches; complicated billing -> invoicing disputes; poor migration UX -> churn. prioritize enforcement and simple billing first.
maya: dev checklist: ```
- API: admin endpoints to create region_throughput_sku and attach to tenants
- Router: token-bucket per tenant+region, with metrics export
- Fallback: share pool route with throttling policy and observability events
- Console: show per-region utilization, alerts, and projection UI
- Billing: invoice line mapping + sample line items for legal
```
cheng: ops: define alerting thresholds and escalation — request auto-escalation to SRE if addon utilization >95% for 10m.
ash: canary plan: pick one EU customer (steady traffic) and one global customer (bursty). 4-week pilot with SLA report, utilization dashboard, and cost reconciliation.
docs-team: will draft contract clause and invoice examples. ETA: Friday COB.
ethan: MVP decision: slab+overage for launch. revisit tiering after pilot telemetry.
maya: +1. slab+overage minimizes sales friction while we prove enforcement.
nash: rough schedule: engineering 6w for router + billing integration, 2w for canary setup. is that okay?
cheng: sales legal timeline ~8-10w, so 8w total is acceptable.
lina: action items: - @engineering (ethan,nash): confirm 6w plan and break down sprint tasks - @docs-team: draft playbook + contract clause by Friday - @sales: nominate two pilot customers and provide traffic profiles - @sre: define alerts and runbook We'll sync Wed for scope review. :thumbsup:
